holidays.name: International Caps Lock Day
holidays.description: TODAY IS THE DAY TO LET YOUR KEYBOARD SHOUT. Hit the Caps Lock key and type everything in capital letters, whether you're excited, angry, or just feeling dramatic. Nobody will be able to tell which one it is.
holidays.origin: Derek Arnold of Iowa created it in 2000 as an internet parody that poked fun at people who overuse all caps. It was first observed on October 22, and June 28 was later added as a second date.
holidays.funFact: It's one of the few holidays celebrated twice a year, on both June 28 and October 22.

holidays.name: National Paul Bunyan Day
holidays.description: A day to tip your flannel cap to the giant lumberjack of American folklore. He is said to have carved out lakes with his footsteps and to have flipped pancakes on a griddle the size of a lake. Babe the Blue Ox is traditionally at his side.
holidays.origin: Paul Bunyan stories began in logging camps and appeared in print in the early 1900s. They were popularized by a 1910s advertising campaign for the Red River Lumber Company, written by W. B. Laughead.
holidays.funFact: Paul Bunyan statues stand in several US towns. The best known is the giant one in Bemidji, Minnesota, built in 1937 and standing beside a statue of Babe the Blue Ox.

holidays.name: National Tapioca Day
holidays.description: A day for the wobbly, pearly comfort of tapioca. Make a bowl of pudding, or sip a bubble tea and chew the chewy pearls through a fat straw.
holidays.origin: It's an unofficial observance of unclear origin, and fans of the sweet, squishy dessert celebrate it each year.
holidays.funFact: Tapioca comes from the cassava root, a staple food in many tropical regions. Tapioca pearls are also the chewy balls in bubble tea.
